title: Copilot code review instructions: nudge the reviewer to run a cheap check before posting behavioral claims, but never require proof
answers: Copilot review keeps posting speculative edge-case findings (off-by-one, breaks on empty input) that it never tested. How do I make it check first?
Where is the instruction that tells the Copilot reviewer to verify claims by running code defined?
Should Copilot review findings be dropped when the reviewer cannot prove them?
How do I change which kinds of review comments the Copilot reviewer is nudged to verify?
body:
Path: .github/instructions/code-review.instructions.md is the instruction file the Copilot code review agent reads. Its "## Verify When It's Cheap" section sits between the knowledge-cutoff guidance and "## Do NOT Comment On", and governs whether the reviewer runs a quick command in the checked-out repo (it has a bash tool on a full checkout) before posting a behavioral claim.
Rule: When a review finding is a behavioral claim that a few seconds in an interpreter could confirm or refute, the reviewer should prefer running the check over inferring. Express this as a short conditional nudge in this file ("Prefer verifying over reasoning whenever it's cheap"), not as a hard requirement that every finding carry proof.
Constraints: Conditional by design: applies only when verification is cheap. Unverified findings stay allowed, because the reviewer has no web access and runs under a small cost budget (per PR description), so requiring proof would suppress useful claims that cannot be checked. Does not change the knowledge-cutoff rules or the review comment format. Applies to Copilot review output, not human reviewers or runtime code.
applies: Copilot PR review behavior configured via .github/instructions/code-review.instructions.md; not MLflow runtime code.
says: Automated pull request reviews post speculative edge case bugs that were never actually tested.
Make the automated code reviewer run a quick check before posting behavioral claims.
Automated review comments keep warning about runtime failures without verifying them in code.
Can we require automated pull request reviews to prove bugs before flagging them?
Prompt the automated reviewer to test suspected edge cases quickly instead of guessing.
search: The Verify When It's Cheap section of .github/instructions/code-review.instructions.md nudges the Copilot reviewer to run quick interpreter checks rather than inferring behavioral claims. Verification is expressed as a conditional recommendation rather than a mandatory requirement that every finding carry proof. Unverified claims remain permitted due to cost budgets and lack of web access. The guidance applies to Copilot review output, not human reviewers, runtime code, knowledge-cutoff rules, or comment formats.
